The Harvest

Three favorites, grown with patience

These are the varieties I stake my name on. I start with the restaurant classics folks ask for by name, and I grow them in small batches so nothing ever sits around getting tired.

Shiitake

Lentinula edodes

Deep, savory, and meaty — the one chefs reach for first. Mine are harvested the day the caps curl just right, so they hit your pan firm, fragrant, and full of that rich umami.

Fresh · Dried · Powder

Cordyceps

Cordyceps militaris

Those bright orange strands are as beautiful as anything in the garden. Cordyceps is the variety folks seek out for their daily rituals — teas, broths, and morning routines — grown slowly and dried with care.

Dried · Powder

Portobello

Agaricus bisporus

Big, hearty caps made for the grill. I let them mature until the gills are dark and the flavor is deep, then pick them by hand so they arrive whole, unbruised, and ready to be the main event.

Fresh

Alongside these, I grow seasonal oyster mushrooms and other functional varieties as the weather and the grow room allow. Whatever's fruiting, I bring — and if you want something special, ask me and I'll try to grow it for you.

How I Care

Every cluster is somebody's supper. I treat it that way.

Growing mushrooms well is mostly about paying attention — every day, in the small details nobody sees. Here's exactly how your mushrooms are looked after, from the first speck of mycelium to the moment they reach your hands.

  1. 1

    Checked by hand, twice a day

    Every bag and block gets looked at morning and evening — temperature, humidity, fresh air, and how the mycelium is running. Nothing grows unattended, and nothing gets ignored because it was a busy day.

  2. 2

    Clean from the very start

    Mushrooms reward a clean grower and punish a careless one. Substrate is prepared carefully, tools and hands stay clean, and any block that shows contamination is pulled immediately — it never gets a chance to touch your food or anyone else's.

  3. 3

    Harvested at the peak, never early, never late

    A shiitake picked a day too soon is a different mushroom than one picked on time. I watch each cluster and take it the moment the caps, color, and firmness say it's ready — then it goes straight into breathable packaging, never sealed up wet and sweating.

  4. 4

    Dried low, slow, and sealed right

    For dried mushrooms and powders, patience is the whole recipe. I dry them gently until they're properly crisp, then seal them right away so the flavor stays where it belongs. No shortcuts, and no tinctures — just fresh, dried, and powdered mushrooms, done honestly.

  5. 5

    Small batches, always

    I'd rather grow a little and grow it beautifully than grow a lot and let the quality slide. When you buy from Champignon de Bayou, you're getting mushrooms one person fussed over from start to finish — and I can tell you exactly how each batch was raised.

The Pantry Shelf

Fresh when you want it, dried when you need it to keep

Fresh harvests

Picked the same week you buy them — often the same day. Fresh mushrooms keep best in a paper bag in the fridge, and I'll tell you exactly how each variety likes to be cooked when you pick it up.

  • Shiitake & portobello for the skillet and the grill
  • Seasonal oysters when they're fruiting
  • Sold at the market and by arrangement for neighbors in 75211

Dried & powdered

Dried mushrooms are the bayou pantry secret: they keep for months, travel anywhere, and a spoonful of powder disappears into soups, gravies, and rice like it was always there.

  • Dried shiitake & cordyceps, rehydrated or ground fresh
  • Mushroom powders for broths, teas, and seasoning blends
  • Sealed in small batches, labeled with the variety and the date

Grow Kits

Take the bayou home and grow your own

The best way to fall in love with mushrooms is to watch them grow on your own counter. My kits are made to teach, not just to sell — every one comes with plain-language instructions and my help if you get stuck.

All-in-One Kit

Everything in a single ready-to-grow block. Cut it, mist it, and watch mushrooms fruit on your counter in about one to two weeks. The friendliest first grow there is.

Includes the grow block, misting guidance, and step-by-step care card.

3-Piece Kit

For folks who want to learn the real process: substrate, spawn, and growing container as separate pieces, so you see how each part works and why it matters.

Includes all three pieces plus a guided walkthrough of the full method.

5-Piece Kit

The full starter setup for someone ready to make growing a habit — more pieces, more control, and room to experiment with a second variety once the first one fruits.

Includes the complete setup, care card, and a standing invitation to ask me questions as you grow.
